run.procedureSummary: Per cycle, each step done line-wide before the next. (1) Feed: add the cycle's feed row to each chamber, ignoring limits. (2) Carry-forward: go chamber 1 to 6 in order. If a chamber is over its limit, cut it to the limit and add the excess to the next chamber, so mass received from upstream counts before that chamber is checked. Chamber 6's excess goes to loss. (3) State: using post-carry masses, a LARVAL chamber at or above its upper mark becomes PUPAL. A PUPAL chamber at or below its lower mark becomes LARVAL. Otherwise no change. Each change is logged. (4) Metabolism: computed at once from the post-state masses. A LARVAL chamber loses floor(m/4), which goes to loss. A PUPAL chamber moves floor(m/2) to chamber i-1, and chamber 1's half goes to loss. A chamber can pass mass back and receive mass from i+1 in the same step. Limits are not enforced here. (5) Moult: if the line total after metabolism is strictly above 38, every chamber becomes floor(m/2) and the removed ceil(m/2) goes to loss. Loss tally = carry-forward discards from chamber 6 + larval burns + chamber 1's PUPAL pass-back + moult removals. The arithmetic was done with a Python script (C:\Users\USER\AppData\Local\Temp\om\desk-250\sim.py). I checked cycle 1 by hand and it matches.

openPoints.point: Which masses the state step compares against the marks
openPoints.assumption: The masses after carry-forward in the same cycle (step 3 follows step 2).

openPoints.point: Rounding of the larval quarter burn
openPoints.assumption: The amount burned is floor(m/4), and the chamber keeps the rest.

openPoints.point: Rounding of the PUPAL half passed back
openPoints.assumption: The amount passed is floor(m/2), and the chamber keeps the rest (the ceiling).

openPoints.point: Rounding of the moult halving (which side the round-down applies to)
openPoints.assumption: The chamber keeps floor(m/2) and the removed ceil(m/2) is discarded to loss. Under the other reading (remove floor, keep ceil), the cycle 1 and cycle 4 figures and everything after them change.
Strictly above 38, using the line total after metabolism. In cycle 5 the total is exactly 38, so the moult does not fire.
Done in a single pass 1 to 6. Mass pushed into a chamber is included when that chamber is checked. There is no second pass, and none is needed because mass only moves forward.

openPoints.point: Metabolism when a PUPAL chamber also receives mass from i+1
openPoints.assumption: All amounts come from pre-step masses and are applied at the same time. A chamber's passed-back half is based on its own pre-step mass only.
Left in place. It is clipped at the next cycle's carry-forward, and after cycle 5 it stays (chamber 4 ends at 7 against a limit of 6, chamber 2 at 10 against a limit of 8).

openPoints.point: The word 'routinely' in the state rule
openPoints.assumption: Read as 'by the normal rule each cycle'. No extra condition.
Chamber 6 carry-forward discards, larval burns, chamber 1's PUPAL pass-back half, and moult removals. Mass moved between chambers is not loss.
